title: Lee Harvey Oswald in the 1963 JFK Record
metaDescription: Lee Harvey Oswald was arrested Nov. 22, 1963 and killed two days later by Jack Ruby. His name recurs in CIA, FBI, and Warren Commission files.
h1: Lee Harvey Oswald in CIA, FBI, and Warren Commission records
lede: Lee Harvey Oswald was the accused assassin of President John F. Kennedy, arrested on November 22, 1963 and killed two days later by Jack Ruby. His name recurs throughout the CIA, FBI, and Warren Commission records in the JFK Assassination Records Collection. BlackVaultDocs’ figure hub matches that name in document titles from public NARA releases. The hub is a name index, not a finding on guilt and not a count of files. PDFs remain on the originating archive.

sections.h2: What the Oswald figure hub lists
paragraphs: The figure slug lee-harvey-oswald groups indexed titles that name Lee Harvey Oswald. The packet supplies no document count for this hub. This page therefore does not invent one. What it can state is the public-record identity in the blurb: accused assassin of President John F. Kennedy, arrested on November 22, 1963, killed two days later by Jack Ruby, with the name recurring in CIA, FBI, and Warren Commission records inside the JFK Assassination Records Collection.

A title match is not the same as a file “about” Oswald in every paragraph. A cable that names him once still matches. A scan that discusses him only in an enclosure may not match if the indexed title omits the name. Researchers who need the page images should open the originating archive from the figure hub. BlackVaultDocs does not re-host those PDFs.

Jack Ruby appears in the same blurb as the man who killed Oswald two days after the November 22, 1963 arrest. Ruby has a separate figure hub. This overlay does not merge the two name indexes. The JFK Assassination Records Collection is the collection named in the packet; it is the internal-link target for the related topic on this site.

sections.h2: CIA, FBI, and Warren Commission as named series, not as a verdict
paragraphs: The blurb states that Oswald’s name recurs throughout CIA, FBI, and Warren Commission records in the JFK Assassination Records Collection. Those three series are named sources in the public files. Naming them is not an argument that any one series is complete, accurate, or conclusive. This page does not rank CIA against FBI against the Warren Commission, and it does not treat title hits as proof of a conspiracy or as proof that no conspiracy existed.

November 22, 1963 is the arrest date in the packet. Two days later is the date Jack Ruby killed Oswald. Those dates are the chronology the blurb gives. This overlay does not add a trial date, a burial date, or a document-count-by-agency split, because those figures are not in the facts.

sections.h2: How name matching works on BlackVaultDocs
paragraphs: Figure hubs match names in document titles from public NARA releases indexed on BlackVaultDocs. The Oswald hub is that match for “Lee Harvey Oswald,” not a biography written from outside sources and not a complete FOIA log. A missing title hit means the indexed title in this ingest did not carry the name as matched, not that NARA never held a file.

The all-figures directory lists other people whose names are similarly matched. The JFK assassination collection link on this packet points at that collection hub. Use the figure page for Oswald-titled rows; use the collection page for the broader posting.

sections.h2: What this page does not claim
paragraphs: This overlay does not adjudicate whether Oswald acted alone. It restates the packet: accused assassin, arrested November 22, 1963, killed two days later by Jack Ruby, name recurring in CIA, FBI, and Warren Commission records in the JFK Assassination Records Collection. Editorial claims that the files “prove” a plot, or that they “close the case,” are outside the index.

No NARA ID is in the packet facts, so none is cited. No document total is in the packet facts, so none is cited. Cite the dates and the named series; do not attach a invented file count to Oswald’s name.

sections.h2: Where to read the indexed titles
paragraphs: The Lee Harvey Oswald figure hub is the live title list. All figures shows the rest of the name index. The JFK assassination collection is the related topic link supplied on this packet. Open the originating archive for scans. If a later ingest retags titles, the hub can gain or lose rows without this prose inventing a number for that change.

sections.h2: How to cite Oswald on this site
paragraphs: Cite Lee Harvey Oswald as the accused assassin of President John F. Kennedy, arrested on November 22, 1963 and killed two days later by Jack Ruby, with the name recurring in CIA, FBI, and Warren Commission records in the JFK Assassination Records Collection, as indexed by title match on BlackVaultDocs. Do not cite a document count from this guide. Do not treat the figure hub as a courtroom finding. The source note is deliberate: figure hubs match names in document titles from public NARA releases indexed on BlackVaultDocs.

A researcher comparing Oswald titles to Ruby titles should keep the two hubs separate. The packet places Ruby only as the person who killed Oswald two days after the November 22, 1963 arrest. It does not give a document count for either name. The JFK Assassination Records Collection remains the collection named in the blurb.

faqs.q: Who was Lee Harvey Oswald in the declassified JFK record?
faqs.a: The packet identifies Lee Harvey Oswald as the accused assassin of President John F. Kennedy, arrested on November 22, 1963 and killed two days later by Jack Ruby. His name recurs throughout CIA, FBI, and Warren Commission records in the JFK Assassination Records Collection. BlackVaultDocs matches that name in indexed titles. This page does not assign a file count.

faqs.q: When was Lee Harvey Oswald arrested and killed?
faqs.a: He was arrested on November 22, 1963 and killed two days later by Jack Ruby. Those dates are the chronology in the figure blurb. The hub does not add a document count for either date. Titles that name Oswald appear on the figure hub; PDFs remain on the originating archive.

faqs.q: Which agencies’ files name Lee Harvey Oswald?
faqs.a: The blurb states that his name recurs throughout CIA, FBI, and Warren Commission records in the JFK Assassination Records Collection. The packet does not split those series into separate counts. This page names the three series as the blurb names them and does not invent a total for Oswald-titled files.

faqs.q: Does the Oswald figure hub prove a conspiracy?
faqs.a: No. The hub matches the name Lee Harvey Oswald in document titles from public NARA releases indexed on BlackVaultDocs. It restates that he was the accused assassin, arrested November 22, 1963, and killed two days later by Jack Ruby. It does not interpret CIA, FBI, or Warren Commission files as proof of a plot.

takeaways: Lee Harvey Oswald was the accused assassin of President John F. Kennedy, arrested on November 22, 1963.
He was killed two days later by Jack Ruby.
His name recurs in CIA, FBI, and Warren Commission records in the JFK Assassination Records Collection.
The figure hub matches that name in indexed titles; this packet supplies no document count.
This page does not treat title hits as a finding on conspiracy or guilt.
